scope: Crate roots, runner binary entrypoint, and contracts for ownership rows 36 through 39

crates.name: jmax-runner
shared_api: Scenario, Step, Expectation, CallRequest, Reply, and Transport
RunnerError with canonical embedded ABI JSON errors

entrypoint.execution: Deterministic offline replay through the library Transport interface
entrypoint.bounds: 16 MiB per input and at most one stored replay body per call or receive step

crates.name: jmax-bench
shared_api: SystemClock with std feature, Sample, BenchmarkReport, Summary
Implemented bounded measurement loop, exact aggregation, nearest-rank percentiles, and stable digests

crates.name: jmax-fuzz
shared_api: NumberMode, NumberConfig, NumberOutcome, NumberCase with optional independent known answers, NumberOracle
DeterministicRng and canonical ABI error helpers

crates.name: jsonmax
shared_api: Canonical ABI reexports and Document alias

contracts.coverage: All sixteen wave modules have exact public signatures, shared type definitions, error conditions, ownership rules, and cross-module invariants documented
contracts.root_snapshots: Each contract embeds the exact corresponding library root source
contracts.integration: Child modules import shared definitions through super::* without sibling-owned shared types
contracts.features: Libraries use std by default and support alloc without std; process child management and SystemClock are std-gated

validation.method: Manual source and contract review only
validation.reason: The task explicitly prohibits build, compiler, formatter, and check commands

constraints.unsafe_code: Forbidden in all four library roots

handoff: Wave module implementations are intentionally not created: they are outside this task's assigned file list and belong to Waves 1 through 4.
Roots and CLI refer to the frozen future module APIs. Compilation and execution remain unverified until those files and dependency implementations exist and a later authorized validation wave runs.
The runner CLI is offline replay. Live reactors can implement Transport; the process lifecycle API is separately frozen in its contract.
Replay bodies have no application error metadata, so ErrorCode expectations require a richer library Transport implementation.
Facade proof creation must delegate to validated native lower layers. Partial query results cannot be promoted directly into validation proofs.
